key_insight: VideoNet introduces a large-scale, domain-focused video dataset and benchmark that restores rigorous evaluation of action recognition for modern vision–language models by emphasizing diverse, temporally grounded, domain-specific actions.
problem_solved: Current VLM evaluations underrepresent true action understanding because existing datasets are too small, generic, or insufficiently temporally/challenging; VideoNet fills this gap by providing diverse, domain-specific action videos and standardized benchmarks to measure temporal and semantic action recognition.
method: Assemble a large, curated video corpus focused on multiple application domains (e.g., medical, sports, industrial) with fine-grained, temporally localized action labels.
Define a taxonomy and annotation pipeline for domain-specific actions, including quality control and temporal segmentation to ensure precise action boundaries.
Provide benchmark tasks, evaluation protocols, and baseline results (standard VLMs and specialized video-action models) to quantify performance and highlight gaps.
impact: By supplying a challenging, domain-aware dataset and benchmark, VideoNet enables researchers and practitioners to better train, test, and compare models on real-world action recognition tasks—driving improvements in video understanding for applied domains like robotics, healthcare, and safety monitoring.
visual_elements: Dataset-at-a-glance card: total videos, hours, domains, and class count (compact icons + numbers).
Sample frames strip: side-by-side short clips or frames showing temporal progression for representative domain-specific actions with labels and timestamps.
Benchmark bar/line chart: performance of popular VLMs vs specialized action models across tasks (classification, temporal localization) highlighting current gaps.
Annotation pipeline flow: schematic showing data collection → labeling → temporal segmentation → quality checks → benchmark split.
paper_title: VideoNet: A Large-Scale Dataset for Domain-Specific Action Recognition
paper_authors: Tanush Yadav, Mohammadreza Salehi, Jae Sung Park, Vivek Ramanujan, Hannaneh Hajishirzi
